title: Redesigning Onboarding for 2M Users
summary: Rebuilt the first-run experience for a consumer app with 2M MAU, cutting time-to-value by 18 seconds and lifting week-1 activation by a third.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body: New users dropped off within the first 90 seconds. Analytics showed 61% never completed setup, and support tickets clustered around unclear next steps. Leadership set a goal: improve week-1 activation without increasing acquisition spend.

sections.heading: Discovery
sections.body: I ran 14 user interviews, mapped the existing funnel, and partnered with design on a jobs-to-be-done workshop. We found users wanted a fast win — not a tour of every feature. The old flow asked for permissions and profile data before demonstrating any value.

sections.text: I just wanted to see if this actually does what I need. Instead it made me fill in my birthday.

sections.heading: My Approach
sections.body: We reframed onboarding around a single 'aha moment': completing one core action in under 60 seconds. I wrote a one-pager with success metrics, ran a phased rollout (5% → 25% → 100%), and built a dashboard tracking activation, retention, and support volume by cohort.

sections.label: North Star
sections.body: Time-to-first-meaningful-action under 60 seconds, measured from install. Every decision in the redesign was evaluated against this single metric.

items.title: One-pager + success metrics
items.desc: Defined activation as 'completes core action within 7 days of install' — aligned with eng, design, and data before a single wireframe was drawn.

items.title: Value-first flow redesign
items.desc: Moved all data-collection steps post-activation. Led 3 rounds of usability testing with 5 users each. Iterated on copy, CTA placement, and progress indicators.

items.title: Phased rollout — 5% → 25% → 100%
items.desc: Monitored activation, D7 retention, and support volume daily at each stage. Gate criteria required ≥15% activation lift before expanding.

sections.caption: Value-first path (right) reduced required steps from 9 to 3 before the core action

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: At full rollout, activation rose 34%, time-to-value dropped 18 seconds, and support tickets for 'getting started' fell 27%. Leadership adopted the value-first framework as the standard for two additional product lines.

sections.label: What I'd do differently
sections.body: I'd instrument the 'aha moment' before starting the redesign — we were flying blind on the exact second users clicked their first meaningful action. Having that baseline from day one would've let us iterate faster in the rollout phase.
